reply_text:
I found one serious bug, so please don't merge yet. The rest of the branch looks fine. I reviewed the diff against main and ran the tests, and they all pass. I didn't change any code.

**Must fix: view-only users can edit (`src/guard.js`, `canEdit`)**
```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```
In JavaScript, `===` is evaluated before `&`. So this line actually computes `share.mask & (WRITE === WRITE)`, which is `share.mask & 1`, and that's the READ bit. I ran it to confirm:
- A viewer share (READ only) gets `canEdit` → **true**.
- A share with WRITE but no READ gets **0**, which is falsy.

Any viewer link can therefore edit any unlocked document. The tests don't catch this because the only editor they check also has READ. The fix is to use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE)`, the same way `canComment` does. I'd also add tests that a READ-only share can't edit and a WRITE-only share can.

**Smaller comments**
- **`transferOwnership` doesn't check who `fromUser` is.** It doesn't confirm that `fromUser === doc.owner`. If it's called with the wrong user, it removes ADMIN from that person and the real previous owner keeps it. Either check this inside the function or make it clear that the caller has to.
- **`toggleRight` allows rights that don't make sense together.** A switch can turn off READ while WRITE or COMMENT stays on, or turn on WRITE without READ. If the dialog should prevent that, nothing enforces it at the moment. If that's intended, it's fine.
- **Missing tests:**
  - turning a switch off in `toggleRight`
  - transferring ownership to yourself (that case works today)
  - `canComment` when the share has no COMMENT right

The changelog entry, the 3.2.0 version bump and the README all match the code. The only exception is the `canEdit` bug, where the code doesn't do what the README says.
